result.topic_en: Argument from the audibility of the sentinels' calls at Portsmouth heard 4–5 miles away at Ryde (Isle of Wight) that, since the mechanical force of sound decreases at least as the inverse square of distance, the ear must respond to wave forces some four million times smaller than at 8–10 feet.
